Figure 8: Ablation analyses of MonteRET and its knowledge-retrieval strategies. a, Ablation study of the key components. -KAR: removing knowledge-augmented retrieval; -VLA: removing vision-language alignment; -RM: removing region masking. b, Comparison of different knowledge retrieval methods. No: without knowledge retrieval; I2I: image-to-image retrieval; I2T: image-to-text retrieval; Class: multi-label classification-based retrieval; MonteRET: proposed knowledge-augmented retrieval module. ns: p > 0.05, *: p < 0.05, **: p < 0.01, ***: p < 0.001, ****: p < 0.0001.

Figure 1: Overall study design and model pipeline. a, Illustration of the multi-granularity modeling of anatomical structures and multi-agent collaboration in report refinement. b, The main components of MonteRET, including a CT report generation module, a knowledge-augmented retrieval module, and a report refinement module. c, Overview of the main experimental design, including dataset, evaluation metrics, and comparison methods.

Figure 6: Comparison of MonteRET with the baseline method across 10 anatomical regions and 18 medical conditions. a, Distribution of the samples in the training set of the RadGenome-ChestCT dataset. b, Clinical efficacy of MonteRET and baseline, measured by micro precision, recall, and F1-score. R01: Abdomen, R02: Bone, R03: Breast, R04: Heart, R05: Esophagus, R06: Lung, R07: Mediastinum, R08: Pleura, R09: Thyroid, R10: Trachea & bronchi. L01: Arterial wall calcification, L02: Atelectasis, L03: Bronchiectasis, L04: Cardiomegaly, L05: Consolidation, L06: Coronary artery wall calcification, L07: Emphysema, L08: Hiatal hernia, L09: Interlobular septal thickening, L10: Lung nodule, L11: Lung opacity, L12: Lymphadenopathy, L13: Medical material, L14: Mosaic attenuation pattern, L15: Peribronchial thickening, L16: Pericardial effusion, L17: Pleural effusion, L18: Pulmonary fibrotic sequela.

Figure 11: Detailed illustration of MonteRET. a, The architecture of MonteRET, which consists of a multigrained feature extractor and a fine-tuned large language model. b, The first stage of model training, where region-level vision and language features are aligned using contrastive learning. c, The second stage of model training, where the large language model is fine-tuned to generate radiological reports based on the extracted vision features and additional instruction prompts. d, During inference, the generated report is further refined by a multi-agent system using a knowledge-augmented retrieval mechanism.

Figure 10: Qualitative results of different methods on representative examples. a, Reference report, and reports generated by the baseline (without the knowledge-augmented retrieval) and MonteRET. b, Regionlevel reports from the reference and generated by MonteRET. c, A failure case. The red and blue colors highlight the errors and correct descriptions, respectively.

Figure 7: Evaluation results from human experts and LLM-as-a-judge (GPT-4o). Each bar represents the number of cases where the corresponding method was rated as strongly unacceptable, unacceptable, slightly acceptable, acceptable, or strongly acceptable.

Figure 2: Comparison of MonteRET against the baseline model without knowledge-augmented retrieval, vision-language alignment, and region masking. a, The RadGenome-ChestCT cohort. b, The NYP/WCM cohort. Clinical efficacy (precision, recall, F1-score) was reported as the micro-averaged performance across 18 common medical conditions. ns: p > 0.05, *: p < 0.05, **: p < 0.01, ***: p < 0.001, ****: p < 0.0001.

Figure 3: Comparison of MonteRET against several state-of-the-art medical methods on the RadGenome-ChestCT test set. Compared methods include R2GenGPT [33], MedVInT [34], RadFM [9], CT2Rep [10], M3D [13], and Reg2RG [5].
